title: Win, Lose, or Hold
bigIdea: Profit and loss are unrealized until you sell.

steps.prompt: Your stock is up $50 on screen, but you have not sold. Did you actually make $50?

options.text: Not yet, it is only on paper until I sell
Yes, the $50 is already in my cash
No, gains never count unless the stock doubles

steps.reveal: A gain you have not sold is unrealized, meaning it is real on paper but can still change. It becomes realized only when you sell.

cards.title: Realized vs unrealized
cards.body: Unrealized profit or loss is the change in value while you still hold. Realized is what you lock in once you sell.

cards.title: Percent vs dollars
cards.body: A $50 gain sounds big, but on a $5,000 position it is 1%. Percent shows the size of a move relative to what you put in.

cards.title: Sell or hold is a choice
cards.body: Selling locks in today's result. Holding keeps you in for more upside, and more risk. Neither is automatically right.

steps.goal: Fast-forward a week on your holding, then choose to sell or hold and see your profit or loss. (Simulation.)

steps.prompt: Sort each statement into realized or unrealized profit and loss.

items.text: You sold your shares for $60 more than you paid
Your held stock shows a $40 gain on screen
You sold at a $25 loss to free up cash
Your stock dropped $10 but you have not sold

steps.explanation: If a trade is closed by selling, the result is realized. If you still hold the shares, any gain or loss is unrealized and can still change.

steps.prompt: You bought 10 shares at $50 each and sold them all at $56. What is your realized profit?
steps.explanation: The price rose $6 per share. Across 10 shares that is 10 times $6, which is $60 of realized profit.
